title: Conditional Execution
definition: Conditional execution selects which instructions run according to the evaluated result of one or more predicates.
purpose: Turn explicit decision rules into inspectable and testable execution paths.
history: Structured programming made selection one of the fundamental control-flow structures alongside sequence and iteration.
mental_model: A program reaches a question, evaluates it once, follows the matching path, and then continues after the selection.
analogy: A railway switch sends a train onto one track; the analogy fails when code contains nested decisions, early exits, or shared continuation points.
industry_notes: Branch structure should preserve the decision model, make default behavior explicit, and permit each meaningful outcome to be tested.
ai_notes: AI-generated branches may be syntactically valid while omitting a decision-table column or placing a broad condition before a special case.
interview_notes: Ask the learner to trace order, identify unreachable paths, and choose inputs for every branch outcome.
